advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'handshake reported ok' from 'the handshake check could not be evaluated' in autodeploy step 5c rather than collapsing both to promote via `|| echo ok`.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:977: print("failed" if hs.get("ok") is False else "ok")' 2>/dev/null || echo ok)"

The inner `try/except` only wraps `json.load(sys.stdin).get("handshake") or {}`; if `handshake` is present but not a dict, `hs.get("ok")` raises AttributeError uncaught, python exits non-zero, and `|| echo ok` promotes.

Mitigated but not closed: step 5 (autodeploy.sh:921-930) already established a 200 from /health within the timeout, so a 5c curl failure is likely transient — but the design intends 5c to be conclusive about the request path.
advisory.finding: The autodeploy handshake gate fails OPEN on any failure of the check itself: `curl ... | python3 -c '...' || echo ok` yields "ok" (promote) when curl fails, when /health returns unparseable JSON, or when the `handshake` value is a non-dict (the `.get` at print time raises outside the inner try). The gate's negative result (promote) is thus indistinguishable from 'the check never produced a verdict', so a transient probe failure at 5c promotes a container the gate was meant to scrutinize.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bracket IPv6 hosts in `_declared_public_host` when appending a non-default port (`[host]:port`).
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:94:     return host if port in (None, default_port) else f"{host}:{port}"
urlsplit strips the brackets from an IPv6 hostname, so re-joining with `f"{host}:{port}"` produces an ambiguous/invalid authority.
advisory.finding: `_declared_public_host` returns the bare `urlsplit().hostname` for IPv6 authorities, so an IPv6 resource-server URL (e.g. `https://[2001:db8::1]:8443/mcp`) yields host `2001:db8::1` and, when a non-default port is present, the malformed Host header `2001:db8::1:8443` (missing the `[...]` brackets an IPv6 host+port requires).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the fail-open behavior of gate 5c (curl error / malformed JSON => promote) is intended, or distinguish 'handshake explicitly failed' from 'could not read handshake' so a broken /health does not promote.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:977  print("failed" if hs.get("ok") is False else "ok")' 2>/dev/null || echo ok)"
Only an EXPLICIT `ok:false` blocks; every error path collapses to promotion, so a container that cannot even render /health cleanly still takes the upstream.
advisory.finding: The new mcp handshake gate (5c) fails OPEN on any curl transport error or malformed /health JSON: `2>/dev/null || echo ok` plus the Python `except: hs={}` both yield "ok", so a new container whose /health returns a truncated body, non-JSON, or errors under load is PROMOTED rather than refused.
scenarios: A new mcp container under memory pressure returns a 500 or truncated /health during the third curl and is promoted.
A JSON serialization regression in handshake_status returns invalid JSON and the gate reads it as promotable.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the mcp store gate at autodeploy.sh:955 from record_backoff_failure to record_mcp_backoff_failure so an mcp store failure does not throttle the review-bot deploy.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:955  record_backoff_failure; exit 1  (inside the mcp store gate 5b)
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:969-970 (new comment) 'Failure records the MCP backoff, NOT $BACKOFF_FILE (which gates the whole script and would throttle a review-bot deploy that never ran this tick)'
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:65-67  '$BACKOFF_FILE gates the whole script at the top, so writing it from the mcp path would let an mcp failure suppress the REVIEW-BOT deploy'
record_backoff_failure writes $BACKOFF_FILE (line 656) which gates the entire script; every other mcp gate uses record_mcp_backoff_failure.
advisory.finding: The adjacent store gate (5b) records the REVIEW-BOT backoff ($BACKOFF_FILE via record_backoff_failure), not the mcp backoff — the exact coupling the new 5c comment declares wrong; this change adds a correct 5c but leaves 5b coupling an mcp failure to the review-bot deploy path.
scenarios: An mcp store-missing failure on one tick writes $BACKOFF_FILE and suppresses the review-bot deploy on subsequent ticks until the mcp target changes.
